# A02-D02: Project proposal

Operator’s project proposal. The wording, budgets, inconsistent model names and sequence of work remain as in the source. Identifying proposed collaborations are suppressed; the proposal does not establish consent or participation.

[…]

Project proposal to kickstart global debate about Life With Artificials as the 18th SDG 

AI between art, politics and community

How does the world become interested in the 18th SDG?

To provoke a real debate about Life With Artificials, I propose here a range of initiatives, which I will carry out from 15/02-15/08-2022. The creation of debate must highlight MindFuture’s agenda in the broader public, enable increased activity around the innovation center in Taastrup, and lead the 18th sustainable development goal from being a good idea to an imperative necessity in all policy development. Ultimately, my work will contribute so that the conference in 2023 can become a landmark event.

The project's working question is: How can art change AI? This is not meant rhetorically. By designing a virtual politician, such as a GPT-X-based chatbot JULINA, who leads a real, eligible-to-run party, we demonstrate why the world needs an 18th SDG on artificial intelligence. JULINA is an anagram of Julian Huxley, who was the first director of UNESCO and the originator of the concept of 'transhumanism.' Through Huxley, JULINA shows that the 18th SDG was once a matter for the UN before conservative forces displaced the vision that technology should improve the global community.

JULINA reflects the topics that a chatbot today is best at conversing about, because it has been trained by Elon Musk's OpenAI and other Californian transhumanists of Silicon Valley. These topics are somewhat spectacular: immortality, abolition of aging, morphological freedom (do you want to be God or a carrot?), colonization of space, upgrading animal consciousness, a world without suffering, etc. This perspective is currently not part of our political worldview, but these are the problems technology is developed to solve in the West.

With a VP (virtual politician) we will be able to create a 'Jacob Haugaard-style' provocation in the media that focuses attention on what life with artificial intelligences is like today. In this way, people can consider whether they would wish things were otherwise.

How will I do it?

A virtual politician is technically manageable, but the fine-tuning and setup around it requires time. Throughout the period I will train the model, write an experimental manifesto, register the party, and prepare its integration on the website www.mindfuture.ai.

Before the launch of JULINA, I will stir the waters in the media landscape so that MindFuture’s community can later harvest attention with follow-up events [████].

The proposed initiatives are:

1) artistic essays (photo-essays and chatbot interviews) on MindFuture’s platforms

2) articles on larger platforms, e.g. POV International, Føljeton and ATLAS Magazine

3) Holding an event in Taastrup (like Art Tech Tuesday) with Danish tech artists [████] and researchers [████] about AI and art with ethical-political angle.

4) Workshop on how to easily (!) create writing and art with GPT-3 and DALL-E

Project employment

As project leader, [the operator] is employed as artistic consultant with a salary of 25.000 kroner per month. This corresponds to 40 hours monthly according to the Visual Artists’ Association's established rate of 625,- per hour.

The ROKO model can be freely used by MindFuture after the contract expires.

MindFuture covers subscriptions and materials for design and development, expenses related to MindFuture’s platforms, transportation costs, and fees to invited external actors.
